measures.title: Parks, recreation, aquatic and open space bonds ($260,000,000) – THIS IS A TAX INCREASE
measures.summary: Authorizes the City to issue up to $260 million in general obligation bonds for citywide park, recreation, aquatic and open space improvements and land acquisition, and to levy property taxes to repay them. The ordinance lists priority projects including the Gus Garcia Recreation Center, Doris Miller Auditorium, Mayfield Park, several trails and parks, four pools, and parkland acquisition.
measures.yesMeans: The City may issue up to $260 million in park bonds and levy taxes to repay them.
measures.noMeans: The City may not issue these park bonds.

measures.title: Library facilities bonds ($35,000,000) – THIS IS A TAX INCREASE
measures.summary: Authorizes the City to issue up to $35 million in general obligation bonds for library facilities and to levy property taxes to repay them. The ordinance gives priority to the existing Hampton at Oak Hill branch library and a new Colony Park branch library.
measures.yesMeans: The City may issue up to $35 million in library bonds and levy taxes to repay them.
measures.noMeans: The City may not issue these library bonds.

measures.title: Charter amendment: Independent Citizens Redistricting Commission
measures.summary: Amends the City Charter to state that the Independent Citizens Redistricting Commission (ICRC) is independent of City Council control and to let it review council districts after the City's boundaries change. It also creates voter-registration and residency-length exceptions for student members, sets an effective date for the ICRC's plan, enlarges the pool of potential appointees, clarifies how vacancies are filled, and lets City staff communicate with the ICRC outside meetings in compliance with the Texas Open Meetings Act.
measures.yesMeans: The listed changes to the redistricting commission's charter provisions are adopted.
measures.noMeans: The charter's current redistricting commission provisions stay as they are.

measures.title: Charter amendment: weekly Council meetings
measures.summary: Amends the City Charter to delete the language providing that the City Council shall meet at least once each week.
measures.yesMeans: The charter would no longer require the Council to meet at least once a week.
measures.noMeans: The charter keeps requiring the Council to meet at least once a week.

measures.title: Charter amendment: Council rules by ordinance
measures.summary: Amends the City Charter to delete the language requiring the City Council to determine its rules and order of business by ordinance.
measures.yesMeans: The charter would no longer require the Council to set its rules and order of business by ordinance.
measures.noMeans: The charter keeps requiring the Council to set its rules and order of business by ordinance.

measures.title: Charter amendment: campaign finance limits and the term "election"
measures.summary: Amends the City Charter to clarify the meaning of the term "election" and to have campaign contribution and expenditure limits adjusted each year by January 1 instead of when the City budget is adopted.
measures.yesMeans: The term "election" is clarified and campaign limits are adjusted each year by January 1.
measures.noMeans: Campaign limits keep being adjusted when the budget is adopted, and the term is not redefined.

measures.title: Charter amendment: timing of initiative and petitioned charter elections
measures.summary: Amends the City Charter so that initiative elections and petitioned charter amendment elections must be held on the next available November election date in an even-numbered year that allows enough time to meet other legal requirements.
measures.yesMeans: Initiative and petitioned charter amendment elections would be held on the next available even-year November election date.
measures.noMeans: The charter's current timing rules for these elections stay in place.

measures.title: Charter amendment: appointment and removal of the City Attorney
measures.summary: Amends the City Charter to provide that the City Council appoints and removes the City Attorney.
measures.yesMeans: The City Council would appoint and remove the City Attorney.
measures.noMeans: The charter's current process for appointing and removing the City Attorney stays in place.

measures.title: Charter amendment: Independent Affordability and Efficiency Initiative
measures.summary: Amends the City Charter to require an Independent Affordability and Efficiency Initiative on a regular basis and before any tax rate increase election. The independent contractor would have to identify annual and multi-year savings that exceed the cost of the contractor's service.
measures.yesMeans: The City would be required to conduct the independent affordability and efficiency review regularly and before any tax rate increase election.
measures.noMeans: No such charter requirement is added.

measures.title: Charter amendment: non-substantive corrections
measures.summary: Amends the City Charter to correct typographical errors, punctuation and sentence structure, and to change or remove language that is moot or unenforceable because state law or a final court order has superseded it.
measures.yesMeans: The listed corrections and removals of superseded language are made to the charter.
measures.noMeans: The charter text stays as it is.
